In summary, our research is concerned with
how cytolytic cells (CTLs, NK cells, and i-NKT cells) deliver secretory lysosomes, containing perforin, to the site of contact with target cells (the immunological synapse).
understanding how cells of the innate and adaptive arms of the immune system deliver cytotoxic proteins to the plasma membrane of target cells.
understanding the mechanism by which CTLs, NK and iNK cells deliver their lethal hit to the immunological target, and how this process is regulated in health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the centrosome plays a key role in polarising exocytosis to the immunological 721.221 cell synapse in cytolytic cells from both the adaptive and innate immune systems.
centrosome polarisation to the plasma membrane at immunological synapse provides a mechanism of precise delivery of secretory lysosome content to the site of target cell recognition.
polarised centrosome docking to the immunological plasma membrane provides an efficient and precise mechanism for the delivery of secretory lysosome exocytosis in cytolytic cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
centrosomes polarise to the immunological 721.221 cell, and the Golgi apparatus, endosomes and secretory lysosome polarise towards the centrosomes.
centrosomes direct secretion from cytolytically active cells of both the adaptive and innate immune systems.
we have demonstrated that the centrosome of NK and iNK cells is also polarised to the centre of the synapse and directs secretory lysosome exocytosis to the synapse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism for polarised exocytic release of secretory lysosome is conserved in all cytolytic cells, and is not specific to CTLs.
centrosomal polarization is a general feature of the immunological synaptic structure.

centrosomal docking is a general feature of cytolytic cell synapses, and that this mechanism of centrosomal docking and microtubule-mediated polarised secretion is used by cytolytic cells in the adaptive and innate arms of the immune system.
